data.title: Pilot a recurring brief before scheduling it
data.summary: Reuse the daily-brief automation pattern with freshness checks, deduplication and a useful stop condition.

facts.text: ChatGPT scheduled tasks can reuse skills. Web and desktop have different data access and runtime requirements; local work requires the computer and app to remain available.

prerequisites: Access to ChatGPT Scheduled with an existing brief workflow; check account, client and workspace availability.
Reuse the daily AI intelligence brief at /automate/ and its existing prompt.
steps: Inspect existing scheduled tasks and reuse the daily brief rather than creating a second schedule.
Run its prompt manually on a fixed time window. Preserve source publication dates and last-checked times.
Deduplicate by canonical URL and claim; separate a new announcement from an old story rediscovered today.
Specify output location, missing-source behavior and notification conditions. Check local versus cloud prerequisites.
Only after a successful pilot, configure the authorized schedule and review its first runs. Stop or revise if sources repeatedly fail.
data.output: a manually checked brief and a proposed schedule with runtime prerequisites
validation: Avoid an empty notification unless a periodic summary was requested.
Mark partial coverage and retain the last successful source-check date.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
No schedule was created or provider run executed. Reuse the existing /automate/#daily-ai-brief pattern; do not confuse a feed refresh with source verification.
data.prompt: Inspect my existing daily-brief workflow and any authorized schedule for [topic]. Reuse the current prompt/template. Run one manual pilot for [time window, timezone and approved sources]. Deduplicate announcements, retain original publication dates and distinguish source checks from collection time. Save the brief with missing-source and freshness notes. Propose cadence, runtime prerequisites and meaningful notification conditions. Do not create a duplicate schedule or enable one before the pilot and scheduling request are complete.
tips: This guide proposes a schedule; reading it does not create one.
Track collection time, publication time and human review time separately.
